title: Binary Logistic Regression from Scratch with Gradient Descent
description: Generate two 2D Gaussian clusters, minimize binary cross-entropy loss with batch gradient descent on augmented features X_aug, and plot the convergence curve and decision boundary.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Draw points around `mean0 = [0, 0]` (`class 0`) and `mean1 = [2, 2]` (`class 1`). Stack them into `X_bin` and `y_bin`, and shuffle with `np.random.permutation(n)`.

Define `sigmoid(z)` and `logistic_loss(theta, X, y)` (average binary cross-entropy with the supplied eps). Define `logistic_gd(X, y, ...)`, which updates `theta -= lr * grad` using `grad = X.T @ (p - y) / len(y)`.
Inside `logistic_gd`, each step computes logits `z = X @ theta`, probabilities `p = sigmoid(z)`, and vectorized cross-entropy gradient `X.T @ (p - y) / len(y)`.

steps.question: Why does line 36 prepend a column of ones `np.ones((n, 1))` to `X_bin` to form `X_aug` (and line 50 do the same for `grid`)?
steps.answer: Prepending a column of `1`s lets `theta[0]` act as the bias (intercept) term inside the single matrix-vector product `X @ theta`.

steps.description: Augment `X_bin` with a column of ones (`X_aug`). Run `logistic_gd` on `X_aug` and `y_bin` with the supplied settings to reach `Final loss: 0.23222309478529818`. Plot both `hist` and the contour map of `sigmoid(grid @ theta)`.
